summary: Tobermorey Airport (TYP/YTMY) is a small remote airstrip serving the community of Tobermorey, a sparsely populated locality in the far northeastern corner of the Northern Territory near the Queensland border. The airport primarily supports general aviation, cattle station operations, and occasional charter flights servicing the surrounding Gulf Country region. Its remote outback location makes it an important link for residents, pastoralists, and essential services in this isolated part of Australia.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Tobermorey Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves general aviation, cattle station operations, and charter flights connecting remote outback communities in the Gulf Country region.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights to Tobermorey?
A: No scheduled commercial services operate to the airport; access is typically via private aircraft or chartered flights arranged through regional operators.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small outback airstrip, facilities are minimal, typically consisting of a basic runway with no terminal building or scheduled aviation services.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Tobermorey?
A: The dry season (approximately May to September) generally offers the most reliable flying weather, as the wet season can cause runway deterioration and reduce visibility.
transport_tips: Access to Tobermorey is almost exclusively by air, as the area lacks major road connections. Travelers typically arrange private or charter flights from larger regional centres such as Mount Isa or Alice Springs. Ground transport from the airstrip to nearby stations or communities must be pre-arranged, as there are no rental car services on-site.
local_tip: Carry extra fuel and water when flying in, as the nearest fuel supplies and amenities are often hundreds of kilometres away on remote cattle stations or in larger towns.
